relatedSnapshot.title: Mailbox billing dispute: $54 monthly inbox charge after five months without a collected payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source**: <url:app.intercom.com> (opened 2026-10-04, assigned to Ellaine Fuente; the customer asked for a human on 2026-10-05)

**Customer**: <email>, owner of workspace "Name 4's Workspace" (org <uuid>, billing account <uuid>, native Autumn).

**Ask**: why he has to pay monthly for the mailboxes/domains. He says he opened them in May, that this is the first time since May he has paid, and asks whether $54 will recur every month. Taxonomy bucket: overcharged. No refund was requested.

**Finding**: the charge is correct and the customer paid it himself. He holds 9 live inboxes (3 domains x 3, DFY, all active and connected) at $6 per inbox per month = $54 per month; the three domains are billed yearly at $15.16 each, paid on 2026-04-29 through 2027-04-29. He paid $99.48 on 2026-04-29 and $54.00 on 2026-05-31. From 2026-06-29 his card declined repeatedly with insufficient funds, nothing more was collected, and the domain+inbox subscription was canceled for payment_failed on 2026-07-13. The mailbox audit flagged the 9 mailboxes unpaid on 2026-09-10; a human sent the unpaid-mailbox reminder on 2026-09-29 naming $54.00 a month and a 6 October deadline; the customer paid $54.00 from his own billing page on 2026-10-05 (audit trail cmr_domain_charge.create, actor = his own user id; the $54.00 charge was captured at 08:39 after one insufficient-funds decline at 08:38). No double billing: the earlier $54.00 invoice (2026-06-29) and the $185.00 Pro invoice (2026-09-11) remain open on canceled subscriptions and cover earlier periods.

**Exposure**: $54.00 collected 2026-10-05 for the period 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-05, matching the 9 paid inboxes. Nothing in the evidence supports a refund or a credit. Two invoices remain collectible on canceled subscriptions: $54.00 (2026-06-29) and $185.00 (2026-09-11).

**Proposed human action**: support explains the pricing to the customer (mailboxes are $6 per inbox per month, domains are yearly) and, if he wants the recurring charge stopped, cancels the three inbox add-ons on the billing account; separately decide what to do with the two open invoices on canceled subscriptions and make sure the mailbox audit re-runs so the workspace stops reading as unpaid. This is a proposal, not a promise.

**Also noted**: in the conversation the assistant told him the October charge was the "first monthly billing cycle catching up" and that June-October were renewals "happening in the background". That does not match the records (April and May were paid, June onward failed).

Full readout and evidence in the Billing investigation document on this ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Paid done-for-you inbox orders stay on "waiting for payment" when the user doesn't return from checkout
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a user pays for done-for-you domains and inboxes but doesn't land back on our page after checkout, the order stays on "waiting for payment" even though the money has left their account. We want the app to notice the payment by itself, so paying users get their inboxes without contacting support and don't lose trust in the purchase.

## Problem

On 11 Oct 2026 the owner of the Company Ten workspace paid $99.32 at 5:19 pm Name 6 for 3 domains and 9 inboxes, and Autumn recorded the payment. The email accounts page still said "Your inbox order is waiting for payment". When he clicked "Complete payment" at 5:24 pm, he got "Something went wrong". If he'd clicked "Cancel order" instead, he could have cancelled an order he'd already paid for, which is what happened in ENG-14226. We marked his order paid by hand at 5:35 pm and it's now setting up.

## Root cause

Only the user's browser confirms a done-for-you order after checkout, so a closed tab or lost redirect leaves a paid order pending, and every button on the pending card then does the wrong thing.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Today
    A[User pays in Autumn checkout] --> B{Browser returns to our page?}
    B -- yes --> C[confirmDfyOrder marks paid, setup starts]
    B -- no --> D[Order stays waiting for payment]
    D --> E[Complete payment: new checkout with same subscription IDs]
    E --> F[Autumn rejects: already in use. User sees Something went wrong]
    D --> G[Cleanup job after 30 min: cancels it without checking payment]
    G --> H[Reconcile job: can bring it back, but only on its own schedule and without renewal prices]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[User pays in Autumn checkout] --> B2{Browser returns?}
    B2 -- yes --> C2[confirmDfyOrder, unchanged]
    B2 -- no --> D2[Order waiting for payment]
    D2 --> E2[Complete payment or Cancel order: check this order's own Autumn subscriptions]
    D2 --> G2[Cleanup job: checks this order's subscriptions before cancelling]
    E2 -- all active --> P[Mark paid once, set renewal prices, start setup]
    G2 -- all active --> P
    E2 -- none --> K[Open checkout or cancel, as today]
  end
```

The check uses the order's own Autumn subscriptions, not the account's overall balance, because leftover balance from an earlier failed order could otherwise make an unpaid order look paid.

## Who's affected

In the last 30 days, 42 Autumn done-for-you orders completed and 1 got stuck like this (the Company Ten order), counted from the read-only production replica on 11 Oct 2026. We don't know how many past orders the cron confirmed without setting renewal prices, because nothing records which path confirmed an order. That count is a follow-up.

## Proposed fix

* Add a reader that checks a done-for-you order's own Autumn subscriptions: one per domain, plus one inbox subscription per domain that has inboxes. It says whether they're all active and not past due.
* Use it in "Complete payment", "Cancel order", the 30-minute cleanup job and the reconcile job. When the order is paid, mark it paid once (guarded so only one caller wins), set the renewal prices and start setup.
* When Autumn can't be read or the subscriptions are only partly there, don't cancel and don't confirm. Show a clear message instead of "Something went wrong".
* Stop `confirmDfyOrder` from re-sending setup for an order that's already setting up, so we can't place a second supplier order.

## Out of scope

* Pre-warmed orders: ENG-14227 owns them.
* A guard against duplicate starts inside the supplier setup job, and repairing renewal prices on past orders. Both are follow-ups.

## Done when

* "Complete payment" on a paid done-for-you order marks it paid and starts setup, opens no new checkout, and shows "Payment received. Setting up your inboxes."
* "Cancel order" on a paid done-for-you order doesn't cancel it.
* The cleanup job doesn't cancel a paid done-for-you order, and still cancels one with no Autumn subscriptions.
* An order whose only "proof" is leftover account balance from another order is never marked paid.
* Two callers confirming the same order at once start setup once.
* Regression tests cover each of these at the confirm, checkout and cleanup seams.

## Implementation context

* Code at dcb9d1b1a4: `createDfyCheckout`, `confirmDfyOrder` and `cancelDomainPurchaseOrder` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts`, `cleanup-stale-orders-cron.ts` and `reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts` in `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/`, and the pending card in `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/domain-provisioning-status.tsx`.
* Evidence: Sentry ACQUISITY-3XD for the "already in use" checkout error.
* The full plan and the review of it are in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Self-serve white-label workspaces cannot buy inboxes or domains: checkout fails before payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Client workspaces under a self-serve white-label partner can't buy pre-warmed inboxes and domains. Every checkout attempt shows "payment failed", no payment is taken, and the setup step sits on "In progress" until the order expires. After this fix the checkout opens on our Whop store, the client pays, and the inboxes are set up like any other order.

## Problem

Reported on 18 September 2026 by Company Three (<domain>) while onboarding their first client workspace, Company Eight. The client picked 6 domains with 3 Name 11 inboxes each and pressed pay four times between 11:24 and 11:30 UTC. Each attempt failed before reaching Whop, so nothing was charged. The order was then auto-cancelled at 11:40 when the domain reservation expired.

No self-serve partner workspace has ever completed an inbox order. Past Whop inbox orders all came from big-client partners (Customer Workspace, Name 12 AI) that have their own Whop store set up with us. Self-serve partners are meant to use our own Whop store, which already works for their subscriptions, credit top-ups and website domains (ENG-11291). The inbox checkout was never updated to do the same.

## User experience

* Today: Cold Email Agent setup > Setup inboxes > choose domains > pay shows "payment failed". The step stays "In progress" and retrying doesn't help.
* After: the same flow opens a Whop checkout for the order total. After payment, the order moves to provisioning and the inboxes appear as usual.
* If our store isn't configured for this purchase, the customer sees a clear "not available" message, not a generic payment failure.

## Done when

* A self-serve partner's client workspace can check out a pre-warmed inbox order, and the payment starts provisioning.
* Big-client partners' inbox checkout behaves exactly as before.
* After payment, cancelling, repricing and refunding the order use the same store the customer paid in.
* One real low-cost order in a self-serve test workspace completes in production and is refunded afterwards (preview environments cannot complete Whop payments).

## Implementation context

* Failure: `Whop is not configured for this billing provider config` (Sentry ACQUISITY-547). The inbox order checkout only reads partner or platform Whop settings saved in the database. Self-serve partners have none, and no platform Whop row exists.
* Our webhook ignores payments on our own store unless it recognises the product. So the per-order plan must be created under our existing Email product, which the webhook maps to the email slot.
* Follow the self-serve rule from ENG-11291: self-serve partners always use our store, big clients always use their own, with no fallback between them.
* Don't add a platform Whop row in the database as a hotfix. It changes store selection for every partner.

relatedSnapshot.title: DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable, blocking re-purchase and leaving the domain store inconsistent
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Root cause

When a Done-For-You domain order fails to provision at the provider, the domain rows are written to `mail_domain` (which has a global unique index `mail_domain_domain_unique` on `domain`) and left in a `failed` or `pending` state. Those rows are never released, so they keep holding the name for the original organization. A later order for the same name throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization" at the claim step, silently drops the overlapping domains, and leaves the new order stuck in `provisioning`.

Separately, a domain that failed still renders in Billing with no Cancel option, and the domain store availability check reads the registrar/provider (which never registered the failed name) instead of `mail_domain`. The result is a failed domain that shows as "available to purchase" while its name is actually still claimed internally.

## Evidence

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` `processCreateColdMailOrder`: claims domains into `mail_domain` (unique on `domain`), throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization: ..." when a name is already held, and on provider failure writes domains to `status='failed'` with the order left `requires_attention` or `provisioning`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`: retries failed inboxes on `requires_attention` orders, but does not release a domain name that failed at the provider and does not recover the duplicate-domain-claim collision.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-08-27)

Domain orders stuck in a non-terminal provisioning state: 17 `provisioning` across 17 organizations, 66 `requires_attention` across 66 organizations, 17 `failed` across 16 organizations. Done-For-You specifically: 3 `provisioning`, 26 `requires_attention`.

Domains in `failed` status with at least one `active` inbox (counted 2026-09-05): 106 domains across 41 organizations.

Paid `requires_attention` orders older than 7 days that hold `failed` domains (counted 2026-09-11): 26 orders across 25 organizations, holding 51 failed domains. Never-retried `error` inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days: 33, across 5 organizations. A 2026-09-10 count of the same cohort returned identical figures.

DFY orders stranded by a stale cross-organization `mail_domain` claim, with no saved provider order id and stale beyond 24 hours (counted 2026-09-23): 5 orders across 5 organizations and 5 users, from the ENG-14139 report. Collision cascade as of 2026-09-23: one stale failed claim is a foreign claim on 4 later DFY orders across 4 organizations, and pending claims written by two stuck orders block 4 further organizations' orders. The wider stuck-in-`provisioning` population is 9 orders across 9 organizations, of which 4 belong to ENG-13308's stall mechanism.

## Fix direction

* Release a failed domain's claim so the name can be re-purchased, and reconcile the domain store's availability check against owned-but-failed domains.
* Stop silently dropping overlapping domains from a new DFY order; fail fast with a clear message to the customer instead.

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox
